title: Interface lemmas bridge logDeriv and MeromorphicOn.divisor for the rectangle argument principle
intent: Reduce the rectangle argument principle — the contour integral of logDeriv over a rectangle equals a finite sum of divisor orders — to a finite sum a downstream theorem can already consume, by routing the proof through three interface lemmas that relate `logDeriv` to `MeromorphicOn.divisor`. The glue never unfolds either definition.

parent.name: rectangleIntegral_logDeriv_eq_sum_meromorphicOrderAt
parent.statement:
theorem rectangleIntegral_logDeriv_eq_sum_meromorphicOrderAt
    {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z w : ℂ}
    (zRe_le_wRe : z.re ≤ w.re) (zIm_le_wIm : z.im ≤ w.im)
    (hf : MeromorphicOn f (Rectangle z w))
    (hlog : MeromorphicOn (logDeriv f) (Rectangle z w))
    (hfinite_order : ∀ p ∈ Rectangle z w, meromorphicOrderAt f p ≠ ⊤)
    (hno_boundary :
      Disjoint (RectangleBorder z w) (MeromorphicOn.divisor f (Rectangle z w)).support) :
    RectangleIntegral' (logDeriv f) z w =
      ∑ p ∈
        ((divisor_support_rectangle_finite f z w).toFinset),
          ((MeromorphicOn.divisor f (Rectangle z w)) p : ℂ)

children.name: logDeriv_residue_eq_meromorphicOrderAt
children.statement:
theorem logDeriv_residue_eq_meromorphicOrderAt
    {f : ℂ → ℂ} {p : ℂ} {n : ℤ}
    (hf : MeromorphicAt f p)
    (hord : meromorphicOrderAt f p = (n : WithTop ℤ)) :
    residue (logDeriv f) p = (n : ℂ)
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: the residue of logDeriv f at p equals the meromorphic order n of f at p, as a complex number

children.name: logDeriv_hasSimplePolesOn_of_meromorphicOrderAt_ne_top
children.statement:
theorem logDeriv_hasSimplePolesOn_of_meromorphicOrderAt_ne_top
    {f : ℂ → ℂ} {R : Set ℂ}
    (hf : MeromorphicOn f R) (hlog : MeromorphicOn (logDeriv f) R)
    (hfinite_order : ∀ p ∈ R, meromorphicOrderAt f p ≠ ⊤) :
    HasSimplePolesOn (logDeriv f) R
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: logDeriv f has simple poles on R whenever f is meromorphic on R and no order equals top

children.name: logDeriv_poles_eq_divisor_support
children.statement:
theorem logDeriv_poles_eq_divisor_support
    {f : ℂ → ℂ} {R : Set ℂ}
    (hf : MeromorphicOn f R) (hlog : MeromorphicOn (logDeriv f) R)
    (hfinite_order : ∀ p ∈ R, meromorphicOrderAt f p ≠ ⊤) :
    R ∩ {p | meromorphicOrderAt (logDeriv f) p < 0} =
      (MeromorphicOn.divisor f R).support
children.closed_by: ext p; constructor; each direction by_cases on the order n = 0 vs n ≠ 0
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: the poles of logDeriv f inside R are exactly the support of the divisor of f on R

children.name: divisor_support_rectangle_finite
children.statement:
lemma divisor_support_rectangle_finite (f : ℂ → ℂ) (z w : ℂ) :
    (MeromorphicOn.divisor f (Rectangle z w)).support.Finite
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: the divisor support of f on a rectangle is finite

applicability.use_when: Two abstraction layers meet in one theorem and the client would otherwise unfold one layer's definitions into the other. Write one bridge lemma per direction of the crossing (residue↔order, poles↔support, order→simple-poles) plus the finiteness fact the sum needs, so the client becomes a chain of `have`s citing them.

consequences: The move creates three named bridge lemmas plus a finiteness lemma, each carrying hypotheses the client must discharge: `MeromorphicAt`/`MeromorphicOn` at every point and the finite-order condition `meromorphicOrderAt f p ≠ ⊤`. The client therefore spends most of its length assembling those hypotheses into the rectangle residue theorem's inputs (`hlog_simple`, `hlog_no_boundary`, `hlog_poles_finite`) before a final `Finset.sum_congr` rewrites each residue as a divisor order. Failure modes: a bridge lemma stated too strongly (e.g. assuming all orders finite when the client only has that on a subset) becomes un-appliable and forces either a weaker lemma or unfolding; the border-disjointness obligation (`hno_boundary`) must be re-derived in the divisor language via `hlog_poles_eq`, which fails if the poles/support correspondence is not already an equality.
